title: Projection transformations commute with compactification refinements
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $c_i=(j_i:X\hookrightarrow\overline X_i,p_i:\overline X_i\to Y)$, $i=1,2$, be compactifications and let $v:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$ be a proper refinement, so $vj_1=j_2$ and $p_2v=p_1$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $F_i=Rp_{i*}j_{i!}$, using exact extension by zero [def-weil-extension-by-zero], and let $\theta_v:F_1\xrightarrow{\sim}F_2$ be the specified normalized compactification comparison of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]. For $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and $L\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ suppose that $K,L$ and $K\otimes_A^LLf^*L$ have the etale-origin witnesses of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], with the last tensor also bounded below. Let $\operatorname{PF}^{c_i}_{f,K,L}$ be precisely the counit-defined compactification projection transformations of [def-exchange-projection]. Then
$$\theta_v(K\otimes_A^LLf^*L)\circ\operatorname{PF}^{c_1}_{f,K,L}
=\operatorname{PF}^{c_2}_{f,K,L}\circ(\theta_v(K)\otimes1_L).$$
Both sides are maps $F_1K\otimes_A^LL\to F_2(K\otimes_A^LLf^*L)$, with the canonical pullback, tensor and direct-image compositors inserted. The same equation holds with $\theta_v$ replaced by the normalized comparison between any two compactifications through a common refinement. This is an equality of the specified finite pro-etale maps on the witnessed domain; it does not assert invertibility of a projection map and requires no constructibility or finite Tor amplitude.

source.place: Sentence beginning Independence of the compactification: compatibility of refinement comparisons with counits and j_!; worker-formulated finite witnessed PF square, with no abstract six-functor datum.

proof.text:
Fix the refinement $v$ and abbreviate $J_i=j_{i!}$ and $P_i=Rp_{i*}$. All of $\overline X_1,\overline X_2$ are of finite type over $k$, hence Noetherian, so $j_1,j_2$ are quasi-compact open immersions and $v$ is proper. The normalized comparison on the witnessed domain is the comparison of [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism], namely
$$	heta_v=P_2( eta_v)\,c_{p_2,v},$$
where $c_{p_2,v}:R(p_2v)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}P_2Rv_*$ is the canonical direct-image compositor of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] and $ eta_v=\Gamma_v^{-1}$, with $\Gamma_v:J_2\xrightarrow{\sim}Rv_*J_1$ the transport along the witness of the pro-etale proper/open map $\alpha_v(L)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-proetale] used in part (a) of that definition. We identify $\Gamma_v$ with the proper/open mate $\gamma$ of [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] for the refinement square $A=C=X$, $B=\overline X_1$, $D=\overline X_2$, $k=j_1$, $i=j_2$, $r=\mathrm{id}_X$, $p=v$. First, for $K=
u_X^*L$ with $L\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$: [lem-sf-proper-open-comparison-site-normalization] writes $\alpha_v(L)$ as $Rv_*(e_{j_1,L})\circ b_{v,j_{1!}L}\circ
u^*(\alpha^e_{v,L})\circ e_{j_2,L}^{-1}$, with $\alpha^e_{v,L}$ the etale map of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. By the refinement clause of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] (case $A=C$, $r=\mathrm{id}$, $k=j_1$, $i=j_2$, $p=v$), $\alpha^e_v$ is its normalized finite proper/open comparison $\gamma^e_Q$. By [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], applied with $B=A$ to the constant strict tower with value $
u_X^*L$ (each level an etale-origin object), the clopen-projection mate $\gamma_Q$ is computed levelwise, and its level is exactly the pro-etale transport of $\gamma^e_Q$ under the canonical comparisons $b$ and $e$; [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] defines its finite-coefficient $\gamma$ by precisely this clopen-projection mate normalization, so $\gamma_{
u^*L}=Rv_*(e_{j_1,L})\,b_{v,j_{1!}L}\,
u^*(\gamma^e_{Q,L})\,e_{j_2,L}^{-1}=\alpha_v(L)$. Second, for a witnessed $(K,L,\alpha)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], $\Gamma_v(K)=Rv_*J_1(\alpha)\circ\alpha_v(L)\circ J_2(\alpha)^{-1}$ by definition, and this equals $\gamma_K$ by naturality of the mate $\gamma$ along the isomorphism $\alpha$. Thus $\Gamma_v=\gamma$, i.e. $ eta_v=\gamma^{-1}$, on $K$ and on the witnessed tensor $K\otimes_A^LLf^*L$. [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] supplies the same normalized comparison on the stated witnessed domain, and [def-exchange-projection] identifies each $\operatorname{PF}^{c_i}$ with the counit-defined proper projection $\pi_{p_i}$ followed by $Rp_{i*}$ of the specified open tensor map.

source.place: Sentence beginning Independence of the compactification: compatibility of refinement comparisons with counits and j_!; finite witnessed specialization.

proof.text:
Apply the normalized proper/open projection-mate identity [lem-sf-proper-open-projection-mate] to the square $A=C=X$, $B=\overline X_1$, $D=\overline X_2$, with $k=j_1$, $i=j_2$, $r=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $p=v$.  Put $N=Lp_2^*L$.  The identity specializes, with the canonical pullback comparison $Lj_2^*N\cong Lf^*L$, to
$$\Gamma_{v,K\otimes Lf^*L}\,j_{2!}(\pi_{\mathrm{id};K,Lj_2^*N})\,\delta_{j_2;K,N}
=Rv_*(\delta_{j_1;K,N})\,\pi_{v;J_1K,N}\,(\Gamma_{v,K}\otimes1_N).$$
Here $\pi_{\mathrm{id}}$ is the identity by the counit definition, and the two $\delta$ maps are exactly the open tensor maps in [def-exchange-projection].  The refinement equations $vj_1=j_2$ and $p_2v=p_1$ are the hypotheses supplied by [def-weil-compactifications-refinements].  By Step 1, every occurrence of $\Gamma_v$ is $\beta_v^{-1}$, including its component on $K$ and on $K\otimes Lf^*L$; hence this displayed mate identity is an equality of the actual normalized open/proper composites used by the two projection transformations.

source.place: Independence of the compactification: compatibility of the refinement comparisons with the counits and with j_!, together with naturality.

proof.text:
The remaining proper factor is $p_1=p_2v$.  Write $c=c_{p_2,v}$ and let $M$ be on $\overline X_1$, $N$ on $Y$.  Expanding the counit-defined map of [def-exchange-projection], the pasted counit formula in [fix-prop-adjunctions] (3), the composition-compatible tensor comparison of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso], and the canonical compositor of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] give the typed composition law
$$c_{M\otimes P_{p_2v}N}\,\pi_{p_2v;M,N}
=Rp_{2*}(\pi_{v;M,Lp_2^*N})\,\pi_{p_2;Rv_*M,N}\,(c_M\otimes1_N),$$
with the displayed pullback and tensor associators inserted.  This is obtained by substituting the pasted counit into the definition of $\pi$; no projection map is inverted.  The same definition says that $\pi_{p_2}$ is natural in its first variable, so its square with $\beta_v:Rv_*J_1\to J_2$ commutes.  Apply the displayed composition law to $M=J_1K$ and $N=L$, then apply $Rp_{2*}$ to the mate identity of Step 2.  Using naturality of $\beta_v$, the two sides become respectively
$$\theta_v(K\otimes_A^LLf^*L)\circ\operatorname{PF}^{c_1}_{f,K,L}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\operatorname{PF}^{c_2}_{f,K,L}\circ(\theta_v(K)\otimes1_L).$$
The first identification uses $p_1=p_2v$ and the second uses $vj_1=j_2$ and $Lj_2^*Lp_2^*L\cong Lf^*L$; these are exactly the canonical compositors in [def-exchange-projection] and [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]. Thus the required square follows from an explicit counit, composition, and naturality calculation.

source.place: Independence of the compactification: compatibility of the refinement comparisons with the counits and with j_!, together with naturality.

proof.text: For a comparison between arbitrary compactifications through a common refinement, apply the preceding equality to each refinement leg and compose.  The identity, transitivity, and cocycle clauses of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], together with the identity and associativity clauses for the direct-image compositor in [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], cancel the intermediate comparison and show that the resulting map is independent of the chosen common refinement.  The same transitivity gives the cocycle for triples, so the equation is unchanged when $\theta_v$ is replaced by the normalized comparison through any common refinement.  All maps are natural on the witnessed domain; only the comparison isomorphisms $\theta_v$ and $\beta_v$ are inverted.

lean.statement: theorem pf_refinement_compatibility (P : WeilConjectures.PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))] (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] (c₁ c₂ : Compactification f) (O_K : PfRefinementOrigin P X) (O_L : PfRefinementOrigin P Y) (O_T : PfRefinementOrigin P X) (hT : pfRefinementTensor P f O_K O_L ≅ pfRefinementObject P X O_T) : (∀ r : c₁ ⟶ c₂, PfRefinementSquare P c₁ c₂ O_K O_L O_T hT (pfRefinementComparison P r O_K) (pfRefinementComparison P r O_T)) ∧ (∀ (d : Compactification f) (r₁ : d ⟶ c₁) (r₂ : d ⟶ c₂), PfRefinementSquare P c₁ c₂ O_K O_L O_T hT ((pfRefinementComparison P r₁ O_K).symm ≪≫ pfRefinementComparison P r₂ O_K) ((pfRefinementComparison P r₁ O_T).symm ≪≫ pfRefinementComparison P r₂ O_T))
lean.note: Exact specialization to PurityFiniteSetting. Helper abbreviations reuse the retained origin category, canonical fixed-scalar realization, and normalized refinement comparison. PfRefinementSquare is the displayed equality expanded from the canonical counit-defined projection maps; the theorem instantiates it for each refinement and every common refinement, without added flatness, constructibility, or Tor-amplitude assumptions.
